diagnostic_features.evidence: The disease develops in three major phases. Red specks are dissolved and the whole base of the spindle gets rotten and dried up. The third stage known as the knife cut stage shows transverse cuts in the rind of the stalk or stem. summary.evidence: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf. Leaves look burned and curl inward, giving them a scalded appearance–hence the disease's name. Ultimately, the entire plant dies.
